chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Muawiya ibn 'Ammar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
If Al-Hamd (Surah Al-Fatihah) were recited over a deceased person seventy times, then the soul were to return to him, that would not be a cause for astonishment.

key_terms.الْحَمْدُ: Al-Hamd (The Praise), referring to Surah Al-Fatihah

ai.seo_question: What is the significance of reciting Surah Al-Fatihah over the deceased in Shia tradition?
ai.summary: Imam Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) states that reciting Surah Al-Fatihah over a deceased person seventy times is sufficient for the soul to return, a feat that would not be surprising. This highlights the spiritual power and efficacy of Quranic recitation, particularly Surah Al-Fatihah, in affecting the state of the deceased. In Shia tradition, this hadith underscores the concept of 'Ruhaniyyat' (spiritual intercession) and the potent barakah of the 'Umm al-Kitab', suggesting that consistent, sincere recitation can influence the spiritual realm and even facilitate resurrection or soul return, emphasizing the Quran's role as a source of healing and life.
